title: Valid Mountain Array
summary: Determine if an array is a valid mountain array by checking if it has at least three elements and contains a peak where elements strictly increase to the peak and then strictly decrease from the peak.
statement: Determine if an array is a valid mountain array by checking if it has at least three elements and contains a peak where elements strictly increase to the peak and then strictly decrease from the peak.
constraints: A mountain strictly rises then strictly falls, with both slopes nonempty.
Return whether the entire array is one mountain.
reference_solution:
def is_valid_mountain(arr):
 if len(arr)<3:return False
 i=0
 while i+1<len(arr) and arr[i]<arr[i+1]:i+=1
 if i==0 or i==len(arr)-1:return False
 while i+1<len(arr) and arr[i]>arr[i+1]:i+=1
 return i==len(arr)-1

hints: Walk the strictly increasing slope, verify a genuine interior peak, then walk down.
A single index can mark the transition between the two phases.
Reject length<3, peak at either endpoint, flats, or leftover positions.
The two scans cover the whole array exactly when both required slopes exist.
